dedupe_keys.name: nrrl list of norwegian amateur radio repeaters

description: The Norwegian amateur radio league, NRRL, publishes a searchable list of Norwegian amateur radio repeaters (relay stations), which it describes as unmanned radio stations that receive signals on one frequency and retransmit them on another, usually placed on mountain tops or tall buildings for the best range; many of the league's local groups run repeaters. For each repeater the list gives the call sign, type (such as FM or DMR repeater), location, transmit and receive frequencies, operating group, Maidenhead locator, access information such as the sub-tone, and status, and it can be filtered, for example by area or frequency; the version read was updated with data as of 10 November 2025, and a team for fixed installations handles changes and applications for new repeaters. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the list depends on reports from the groups and is a web table, not a download. Coverage is Norway. It supports analysis of backup and emergency radio communications that do not depend on public telecom networks, which the league's emergency communications service (Sambandstjenesten) uses; related records are the REF lists of French repeaters and beacons and the ÖVSV repeater and digipeater database.
